title: The Thirukkural
author: Tiruvalluvar
translator: V. V. S. Aiyar, 1916 (public domain; archive.org)
blurb: 1,330 two-line couplets from Tamil Nadu on virtue, wealth and love — the 'universal scripture' of South India.

knowledge.e: Her knowledge of plants saved the garden.

instinctively.e: He instinctively ducked when the ball flew past.

cards.title: A is the first letter
cards.text: The Kural opens with a famous image: as 'A' begins every alphabet, so the divine begins everything that exists.
cards.quote: A is the starting-point of the world of sound
cards.qLife: Every great journey begins with a first, simple step.
cards.orig:
IN PRAISE OF THE LORD

1. A is the starting-point of the world of sound : even so is the Great Original the starting-point of all that exists.

2. Of what avail is all thy learning if thou worship not the holy feet of Him of the perfect intelligence ?

3. Whoso taketh refuge in the sacred feet of Him whose walk is among flowers, his days will be many upon the earth.
cards.origFrom: Tiruvalluvar, The Kural (tr. V. V. S. Aiyar, 1916)

cards.title: Why choose harsh words?
cards.text: Using hard words when gentle ones would work is like choosing unripe fruit over ripe.
cards.quote: Behold the man who useth hard words when sweet ones serve : he preferreth the unripe fruit to the ripe.
cards.qMean: Choosing harsh words over kind ones is foolish.
cards.qLife: Snapping at a waiter when a polite word would work better.
cards.orig:
98. Words that are kind and are removed from all littleness yield good in this life and in the next also.

99. Why doth not a man cease from violent words, even after he hath felt the sweetness that kind words give ?

100. Behold the man who useth hard words when sweet ones serve : he preferreth the unripe fruit to the ripe.

cards.title: Shame them with kindness
cards.text: The best punishment for those who hurt you: do them a good turn, so they feel ashamed.
cards.quote: Let him do them a good turn and make them ashamed in their hearts.
cards.qMean: Answer people who hurt you with kindness.
cards.qLife: Helping a neighbour who once complained about you.
cards.orig:
313. If thou injure another, even though it be only a man who hath injured thee without any provocation, thou simply bringest down upon thyself evils that can never be remedied.

314. How shall a man punish them that have injured him ? Let him do them a good turn and make them ashamed in their hearts.

315. Of what avail is intelligence to a man if he doth not look on others’ pain as his own and abstain from injuring any ?
cards.origFrom: Tiruvalluvar, The Kural (tr. V. V. S. Aiyar, 1916)

cards.title: Knowledge is a spring
cards.text: Knowledge is like water from a sand-spring: the more you dig, the more freely it flows.
cards.quote: Knowledge is like unto a sand-spring: the more thou diggest and drawest thereat, the more excellent is the flow thereof.
cards.qMean: The more you learn, the more you're able to learn.
cards.qLife: Learning a second language makes the third easier.
cards.orig:
THE KURAL

396. Knowledge is like unto a sand-spring: the more thou diggest and drawest thereat, the more excellent is the flow thereof.

397. Everywhere is his home to the learned man, and everywhere his native land : why then doth a man neglect instruction up to his dying day ?

398. The learning that a man hath acquired in one birth will exalt him even in all his succeeding incarnations.
cards.origFrom: Tiruvalluvar, The Kural (tr. V. V. S. Aiyar, 1916)

cards.title: Saying vs doing
cards.text: Anyone can say a thing; doing it as promised is rare.
cards.quote: To say a thing is easy for any man : but to do it in the manner undertaken is a rare thing indeed.
cards.qMean: Talking is easy; doing what you promised is rare.
cards.qLife: Everyone plans to start the gym; few actually go.
cards.orig:
663. The man of action letteth his purpose appear only when that purpose is achieved : for an untimely disclosure would create obstacles that cannot be surmounted.

664. To say a thing is easy for any man : but to do it in the manner undertaken is a rare thing indeed.

665. Behold the man who hath acquired a name for the doing of great deeds : his services will be greatly in request with the prince and will be esteemed by all*
cards.origFrom: Tiruvalluvar, The Kural (tr. V. V. S. Aiyar, 1916)

cards.title: Like a hand catching a slipping cloth
cards.text: A true friend rushes to help in trouble as instinctively as your hand grabs a garment blown loose.
cards.quote: Behold the hand of the man whose garment bath been blown aside
cards.qMean: A real friend helps instantly, without being asked.
cards.qLife: The friend who shows up at the hospital before you call.
cards.orig:
788. Behold the hand of the man whose garment bath been blown aside, how it hurrieth to re-cover his limbs : that is the symbol of the true friend that hasteneth to succour a man in his mis* fortune,

789. Where doth friendship hold its court ? It is where two hearts beat in perfect unison and combine to lift each other up in every possible way.
cards.origFrom: Tiruvalluvar, The Kural (tr. V. V. S. Aiyar, 1916)
